But despite the pitiful state into which the country had descended, the major outside powers, Russian and the Ottoman Empire, did not intervene as they had in 1722-1725. It was partly that they were busy elsewhere, and surely also that the outcome of their previous attempts had not encouraged them to repeat the experiment.
That is from Michael Axworthy's [A History of Iran: Empire of the Mind](https://marginalrevolution.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=7eb0f2150e925f739532ebd3e93a0b6bd7fb29f56a5ecced959e3a5e4308571f&blog_id=42693868&post_id=92826&user_id=262258391&subs_id=225460721&signature=fcf396533d42c0944baca588c70d2516&email_name=new-post&user_email=ishan.mail@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=671c6264bafa58ec556267ba477864a7), a good general introduction to the history of the country.
